findings.title: The phone layout does not reflow, so the page scrolls sideways and the text is a column of single words

location.description: the lead paragraph, squeezed beside the search card on the phone

findings.viewer_experience: A visitor on a phone has to pan sideways to reach the form and read the pitch one word at a time. On tablet the lead runs about 24 characters per line because the card takes half the width.

current.value: page 587 px wide in a 390 px viewport; lead 9.1 characters per line over 18 lines

findings.target: No sideways scroll; one column below a breakpoint: headline, lead, search card, then routes; compact nav
findings.fix_direction: Stack everything in one column below a breakpoint: headline, lead, search card, then routes. Give the nav a compact form. On tablet, stop the card taking half the width so the lead gets a readable line length.

closed_when.check: page_width equals the viewport width in the phone viewport, and characters_per_line of p.lead in the phone and tablet viewports is well above 9 and 24

findings.title: The headline is the quietest text on the page

location.description: the headline above the lead paragraph

findings.viewer_experience: The line that says what the business does reads as a caption to its own paragraph, and the eye goes to the menu and the button instead.

current.value: 22 px, weight 400, #6b7574 at 4.46:1; nav 20 px at 12.75:1; lead 20 px

findings.target: h1 clearly the largest and darkest text, with a real step above the lead and a heavier weight; nav at 16 px; about three levels: headline, 16 to 20 px text, 14 px labels
findings.fix_direction: Make the h1 clearly the largest and darkest text, with a real step above the lead and a heavier weight. Bring the nav down to the 16 px body size so it stops competing.
findings.source: Tschichold, The New Typography; Dair, Design with Type ch. 8-9; Bringhurst 3.1.1

closed_when.check: font_size of h1 is larger than the lead and nav, h1 weight is heavier than 400, h1 contrast is higher than the lead's, and nav.site-nav font_size is 16, in all viewports

findings.title: Two calls to action for one job, in two styles

location.description: the filled green "See boats and dates" button in the hero; the outlined "Search" button is in the card

findings.viewer_experience: The visitor has to work out which button to use and whether they differ. The real primary action, Search with the base, date, nights, and berths already set, looks secondary.

current.value: hero button filled green; Search outlined in the same green

findings.fix_direction: Make Search the filled primary, and either remove the hero button or turn it into a text link that scrolls to the form on small screens.
findings.source: Material Design 3 and Apple HIG button emphasis

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees one filled primary button, Search, and the hero button either gone or shown as a text link, in all viewports

findings.title: The page falls apart into three pieces with dead space between them

location.description: the empty band between the hero and the routes heading; on widescreen the card sits at the far right

findings.viewer_experience: The routes look like a separate leftover, not part of the plan-your-trip story. On widescreen the eye has to travel across empty space to reach the form.

current.value: about 270 px gap between the button (ends y 338) and the h2 (y 612); on widescreen the card at x 1539 with about 850 px between it and the 600 px text column

findings.target: gap above the routes no larger than other gaps on the page; card kept near the text on widescreen
findings.fix_direction: Cap the content width so the card stays near the text. Close the gap above the routes so they read as the next step from the selected base.
findings.source: Arnheim, Art and Visual Perception, ch. I and II

closed_when.check: the distance from the bottom of a.button to the top of h2 in the desktop viewport is close to the page's other gaps, and the left edge of div.search-title in the widescreen viewport is much closer to the right edge of p.lead than 850 px

findings.title: No picture of a boat or the canal

location.description: the whole page, which has no picture

findings.viewer_experience: The copy makes a good factual case, but nothing shows what a week on a narrowboat looks like, so nothing makes the visitor want to go.
findings.target: real photos of the actual boats or routes set into the hero, not a stock or generic image
findings.fix_direction: Set real photos of the actual boats or routes into the hero. The maker must supply the photos.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees a real photo of a boat or route in the hero in all viewports

findings.title: The h1 and the route details are just below the 4.5:1 contrast minimum

location.description: the h1 and the route details such as "7 nights, 38 locks"

findings.viewer_experience: Low-vision readers lose the headline and the route details.

closed_when.check: contrast of h1 and the route detail spans (ul > li > span:nth-of-type(2)) in all viewports is 4.5 or more

findings.title: The nav does not mark the current page
findings.viewer_experience: The visitor cannot tell which page they are on.

current.value: no cue for the active item

findings.target: one cue on the active item, such as a bolder weight or an underline
findings.fix_direction: Add one cue, such as a bolder weight or an underline, for the active item.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees one nav item marked as current in all viewports

findings.title: The input and select borders look pale gray on white

location.description: the borders of the select and input fields in the search card

findings.viewer_experience: The fields are hard to see as fields.

current.value: pale gray on white, not measured

findings.target: border contrast of at least 3:1 against the card
findings.fix_direction: Measure the borders against the 3:1 minimum for component edges and darken them if they fall short.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic judges the field borders clearly visible against white, at 3:1 or more, in all viewports

findings.title: "Start date" is a text field with no year and no visible picker
findings.viewer_experience: Visitors can type an invalid or unclear date.

current.value: text field showing "Sat 14 June", no year, no picker

findings.target: a date input that accepts only valid dates
findings.fix_direction: Use a date input so visitors cannot type an invalid or unclear date.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees the Start date field as a date input with a visible picker and the year shown, in all viewports

findings.title: On the phone the search sits at the top right, in the part of the page that overflows

location.description: the "Find a boat" card on the phone

findings.viewer_experience: The main action is out of easy reach.

current.value: card at x 270, running to x 564 in a 390 px viewport

findings.target: search straight after the lead once the layout stacks
findings.fix_direction: Once the layout stacks, put the search straight after the lead.

closed_when.check: in the phone viewport, div.search-title is within 390 px of the left edge and its top is just below the bottom of p.lead
